title: Standardized Configuration Exchange for Logistics
business: Logistics providers managing cross-platform shipment tracking data.
problem: Inconsistent data parsing across heterogeneous systems leads to unpredictable behavior when duplicate keys or non-standard numeric precision are encountered in configuration files.
solution: Adopting the RFC 8259 JSON format ensures a lightweight, language-independent interchange standard that enforces strict grammar for objects, arrays, and primitive types, promoting interoperability.
steps: Define a schema ensuring all object member names are unique to prevent unpredictable parsing behavior.
Serialize configuration data using UTF-8 encoding without byte order marks to maintain cross-system compatibility.
Restrict numeric values to IEEE 754 double-precision ranges to ensure consistent interpretation across different language runtimes.
Implement a parser that validates the JSON text against the six structural characters defined in the grammar.
outcome: Reliable, predictable data exchange between disparate logistics services, minimizing runtime errors during configuration loading.
limitation: The format does not guarantee identical behavior for non-unique object keys; developers must verify key uniqueness during the generation phase to ensure consistent downstream processing.
